name: Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia with MECOM Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, hematological, and genetic findings

criteria.description: Severe thrombocytopenia presenting in early infancy
Bone marrow examination showing absent or severely reduced megakaryocytes
Identification of pathogenic MECOM gene mutation by genetic testing
Progressive pancytopenia or bone marrow failure developing over time
Positive family history of thrombocytopenia or bone marrow failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe thrombocytopenia with absent megakaryocytes on bone marrow plus confirmed pathogenic MECOM mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other inherited thrombocytopenias and bone marrow failure syndromes

laboratory: Severe thrombocytopenia with normal to low white blood cells and hemoglobin
Bone marrow biopsy showing absent or markedly reduced megakaryocytes
imaging: Radiographs showing skeletal abnormalities such as radioulnar synostosis
Echocardiogram if congenital heart defects suspected
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: May have mutations in MPL gene
Similar bone marrow findings but different genetic etiology
Presence of chromosomal breakage on diepoxybutane test
Characteristic physical anomalies (e.g., short stature, skin pigmentation)
Bone marrow failure with pancytopenia but distinct genetic mutations

redFlags: Severe thrombocytopenia presenting at birth or early infancy
Progressive bone marrow failure with pancytopenia
Family history of early-onset bone marrow failure or thrombocytopenia
references: Ballmaier M, Germeshausen M. Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia: clinical and molecular aspects. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2011;2011:276-282.
Woods GM, et al. MECOM mutations in inherited bone marrow failure syndromes. Blood. 2017;130(10):1233-1244.
